notes: The Leonardo catalogue entry lists no ports; I used names matching the board silkscreen: 2-6, 5V, GND.

Breadboard bank naming follows the catalogue: 't' = rows a-e, 'b' = rows f-j. In the image rows f-j are the upper half (where the 5V wires land) and rows a-e are the lower half (where the signal wires and resistors sit). The pushbuttons straddle the centre gap.

Pushbutton pins: 1.l/1.r are taken as the upper side (rows f) and 2.l/2.r as the lower side (rows e). The +5V wire goes to the upper right leg and the signal and resistor are on the lower left leg, so the switch connects 5V to the signal column.
Column numbers are read from the image: button legs at columns 6/8, 11/13, 16/18, 21/23, 26/28. Pull-down resistors are in columns 6, 11, 16, 21, 26 of the lower half.

Power-rail hole numbers (tp.n, bn.n) are approximate, read from pixel positions. The red wire from 5V goes to the top + rail (tp). Five short red jumpers carry 5V from the rail to the upper leg of each button. The black wire from GND goes to the bottom - rail (bn), and the resistors' other legs go to that rail.
Resistors are 10k ohm (value=10000) pull-downs. Buttons connect pins 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 in order from left to right, as the image shows.
